text:
### Observed differences

- A06 became far more frequent and moved earlier: in the earlier window it appears in about 24 in 100 traces, around the middle of the case (mean relative position about 0.50, upper quartile 0.91); in the later window it appears in about 73 in 100 traces, early in the case (mean about 0.25, upper quartile 0.26, much less variable). [POS001]
- A06's successors collapsed onto a single edge: before, its outgoing transitions were spread over many activities (largest shares A15 about 21 in 100, A47 about 15, A45 about 12); in the later window about 88 in 100 go to A16, which follows within one step in about 97 in 100 observed pairs (before, a one-step gap held for only about 18 in 100). [DIR001, LAG002]
- A previously optional segment became near-universal: A19, A20 and A25 each ran in about 47–48 in 100 traces in the earlier window, but in about 199 of 200 traces in the later window. [REL018, REL019, REL022, DIR004, DIR005]
- That segment now runs in a rigid order after A41: in the later window A41 precedes A19 in about 97 in 100 co-occurring traces (one step later in about 98 in 100), A25 two steps later (about 96 in 100), A20 three steps later (about 95 in 100) and A26 four steps later (about 93 in 100); among themselves, A19 precedes A25 (about 99 in 100) and A25 precedes A20 (about 98 in 100). Before, A41 split its outgoing transitions between A26 (about 45 in 100) and A19 (about 37 in 100), and these pairs co-occurred in only about 47–48 in 100 traces. [DIR006, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL025, REL026, LAG018, LAG019, LAG020, LAG021]
- A06 is now wired in front of this block: it precedes A19, A20, A25, A26 and A41 in about 65–67 in 100 co-occurring traces (before, about 6–12 in 100, with co-occurrence of A06 and these activities rising from about 13 in 100 traces to about 73 in 100); A14 precedes A06 in about 69 in 100 traces and A15 often does too, and A15 now leads to A06 in about 40 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (before, about 94 in 100 went to A16). A06's relation to A16 is mixed (A06 first in about 36 in 100 traces, interleaved or repeated in about 34), but the direct A06→A16 step is immediate when it occurs. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, DIR003, LAG006, LAG009]
- The wider group is now executed together: pairs among A14, A15, A16, A19, A20 and A25 co-occurred in about 47–48 in 100 traces before versus about 199 of 200 in the later window, with fixed orders (for example A14 before A19/A20/A25 in about 97–98 in 100). [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL015, REL018]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, a segment that previously ran in only about half of the cases became a standard, rigidly ordered part of almost every case: A41 is now followed almost exclusively by A19, then A25, then A20, with A26 last, whereas before, A19/A20/A25 each ran in about 47–48 in 100 cases and A41 split between A26 and A19. Together with this, A06 — previously a rare (about 24 in 100 cases), mid-case activity with varied successors — now occurs in about 73 in 100 cases, early, typically preceded by A14/A15 and followed almost exclusively by A16. The signs are direct and mutually consistent: participation and position of A06 [POS001], routing collapses at A06 and A41 [DIR001, DIR006], and relational evidence showing the pairs moved from "mostly not co-occurring or mixed order" to "co-occurring in a fixed order" [REL001, REL004, REL009, REL018, REL021, REL025, LAG002, LAG018, LAG020, LAG021]. The screening count (57 qualifying items against roughly 0.62 expected for an unchanged process, each item also exceeding about 199 of 200 random re-splits) shows the pattern as a whole is far beyond chance. Limitations: the many agreeing items largely describe one underlying trace behaviour and are not independent confirmations; several lag comparisons rest on only about 7–12 before-window observations; and the evidence cannot rule out that the later window simply contains a different mix of pre-existing case variants rather than a modified process. [POS001, DIR001, DIR006, REL004, REL018, LAG002]

Other differences:
- A26, present in every trace in both windows, sits slightly later in the later window (mean relative position about 0.41 to 0.44). [POS002]
- Already-dominant edges became somewhat more concentrated: A14→A15 about 85 to 97 in 100, A44→A45 about 85 to 95, A46→A47 about 91 to 97 of outgoing transitions. [DIR002, DIR007, DIR008]
- Some lag distributions shifted by roughly one step (for example A14→A41 and A15→A41 about one step later); a few lag items have almost no after-window support (a single observation for A15–A26 and A16–A26) and are too thin to interpret. [LAG008, LAG013, LAG012, LAG017]
